explain.say: Here is a feelings meter. The needle points at cross. Tools can bring it back to calm: a slow breath, asking what next, looking at a calendar, or squeezing hands. Well done! Your challenge: pick your favourite tool.

faq.q: Why do I feel upset when plans change?
faq.a: Your brain got ready for the plan. A change means it has to get ready again, and that can feel hard. It is okay to feel that way.

faq.q: What can I say when plans change?
faq.a: You can say, What will we do instead? or When can we do it? Knowing the new plan helps you feel calmer.
asks: Tell me about Breathe and ask
Tell me about Ask what next

faq.a: Plans change because of weather, traffic, someone being ill or a place being closed. Usually nobody chose it.

faq.q: How can I get ready for changes?
faq.a: A picture calendar shows the plan. A grown-up you trust can help you add a maybe card for things that might change.
asks: Tell me about Look at calendar

faq.q: How do other people feel when plans change?
faq.a: Often they feel disappointed too. You are not the only one. You can feel it together.
asks: Tell me about Dad feels sorry

facts: Plans can change for many reasons, like weather, traffic or a closed building.
Knowing the new plan can help a person feel calmer after a change.

quiz.say: Mei's park plan changes. What can she ask?
quiz.why: Asking about the new plan helps her know what is coming.

wrong.1: It is not always her. Plans change for everyone.
wrong.2: Asking helps more than staying quiet.

quiz.say: Why was there no park today?
quiz.show: Why was there no park today?
quiz.why: The weather changed the plan. It was nobody's fault.

wrong.1: Mei did nothing wrong. The rain changed it.
wrong.2: Dad was sorry too, not cross.
